summary_paragraph: A man with a history of COPD, prior stroke, coronary artery disease with bypass, hypothyroidism, and alcohol use disorder was admitted for epigastric pain and vomiting worsened by eating. He had a history of severe esophagitis, and CT imaging confirmed esophagitis with wall thickening and mucosal enhancement. Cardiac workup showed no acute ischemia, and chest pain was attributed to esophageal irritation. He was started on ranitidine and sucralfate, with continuation of home medications including clopidogrel, atorvastatin, and acamprosate. Delirium noted on admission resolved spontaneously. He was discharged home with instructions to follow up with his primary care provider for outpatient endoscopy and stress testing, and to avoid alcohol and irritants.
